goal_evaluations.evidence_quote: It's too noisy. I need my headphones. / I'm ready. Back to the worksheet.
goal_evaluations.analysis: Marcus independently requested noise-canceling headphones during a noisy period (~7:20 into session) and returned to the math task in under three minutes. After a peer conflict at the first incident flag, he again chose headphones and resumed work rather than exiting the room.

goal_evaluations.evidence_quote: You got seven of eight correct on the regrouping set — that's about eighty-seven percent.
goal_evaluations.analysis: On a double-digit addition-with-regrouping probe, Marcus scored 7/8 (87%), meeting the 80% accuracy criterion for this session. He identified the carry error on item five during review.

incident_analysis.antecedent: Peer demanded Marcus's eraser and escalated verbally while Marcus was reviewing a math error with the teacher.
incident_analysis.behavior: Marcus raised his voice, refused to give the eraser, and told the peer to leave him alone.
incident_analysis.consequence_intervention: Teacher coached a breath, redirected the peer to return the eraser and give space, offered break corner or headphones; Marcus chose headphones and returned to finish math.

incident_analysis.antecedent: Teacher directed transition from math worksheet to reading centers; Marcus reported buzzing lights and stomach discomfort.
incident_analysis.behavior: Marcus refused to move initially and voiced sensory/somatic distress.
incident_analysis.consequence_intervention: Teacher validated the sensory report, offered the soft-lamp seat at table two plus a three-minute calm-down timer; Marcus accepted and transitioned.

general_session_summary: 45-minute morning block focused on double-digit addition with regrouping. Marcus met his academic accuracy target (87% on probe) and demonstrated independent use of headphones as a calming strategy twice, returning to task within the five-minute goal window. Two flagged incidents (peer property conflict; transition/sensory load) were de-escalated with teacher-supported choice-making; no full room exit required.
